title: O Lord of Heaven and Earth and Sea
description: O Lord of Heaven and Earth and Sea in Tonic Solfa to HANFORD (SULLIVAN), doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: Christopher Wordsworth wrote these words. They were printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (St. Louis, 1927), as hymn 357.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked 8.8.8.4, to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to HANFORD (SULLIVAN); any other 8.8.8.4 tune fits them as well.
underlay: O Lord of heaven and earth and sea, To Thee all praise and glo-ry be; How shall we show our love to Thee, Who giv-est all?

lines: O Lord of heaven and earth and sea,
To Thee all praise and glory be;
How shall we show our love to Thee,
Who givest all?
Thou didst not spare Thine only Son,
But gav’st Him for a world undone,
And freely with that Blessed One
Thou givest all.
Thou giv’st the Spirit’s holy dower,
Spirit of Life and Love and Power,
And dost His sevenfold graces shower
Upon us all.
For souls redeemed, for sins forgiven,
For means of grace and hopes of heaven,
What can to Thee, O Lord, be given,
Who givest all?
We lose what on ourselves we spend;
We have, as treasure without end,
Whatever, Lord, to Thee we lend,
Who givest all.
Whatever, Lord, we lend to Thee
Repaid a thousandfold will be;
Then gladly will we give to Thee,
Who givest all.

licence: Public domain: Christopher Wordsworth died in 1885.
credits: Words by Christopher Wordsworth (1807–1885), public domain, as printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (1927); set to HANFORD (SULLIVAN) by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
